label: prop:coulomb-strong-ratio-q-rational
title: Coulomb/strong ratio $\tanh(\ln q)$ is the q-rational $(q^2-1)/(q^2+1)$
html:
For every real q > 0 (the substrate-anchor regime, \mathrm{Im}(q) = 0 at the archimedean place), the ratio satisfies:

  \tanh(\ln q) \;=\; \frac{q - q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}} \;=\; \frac{q^2 - 1}{q^2 + 1}.

On a positive braid closure the antisymmetric-to-symmetric ratio of the Coulomb charge equals the q-rational expression (q_0^2 - 1)/(q_0^2 + 1) at the substrate anchor. The analytic and the algebraic forms are a single object.

Significance

The antisymmetric-to-symmetric ratio equals \tanh(\ln q) on a positive braid closure — that is, at n_- = 0; for mixed crossing signs it acquires the multiplicity factor \tfrac{n_+ + n_-}{n_+ - n_-} and is not a constant of the framework (decomposition, item 4). This proposition confirms that on that locus the analytic and the algebraic forms coincide identically over real q > 0. The identity below is independent of that scoping: it is a statement about \tanh, and holds for every real q > 0 whatever the crossing counts. This removes any ambiguity regarding whether the framework employs a "classical-\tanh" or a "q-deformed \tanh_q" realization at the substrate anchor.

The forms match because \exp(\ln q) = q for q > 0. Therefore,

  \tanh(\ln q)
  \;=\; \frac{e^{\ln q} - e^{-\ln q}}{e^{\ln q} + e^{-\ln q}}
  \;=\; \frac{q - q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}}
  \;=\; \frac{q^2 - 1}{q^2 + 1}
  \quad\text{(multiply numerator and denominator by \(q\)).}
